# Example datasets

Two example datasets ship with the package, one per station type. They
are raw station exports, before any processing.

```{r function-datasets}
#' Example Visits from NEDAP Feeding Stations
#'
#' Raw visit records exported from two NEDAP feeding stations.
#'
#' @filename datasets
#'
#' @format A data frame with 31,863 rows and 9 columns:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{animal_number}{Full animal number.}
#'   \item{lifenumber}{Life number (empty in this export).}
#'   \item{responder}{Transponder number. `NA` for visits where no
#'     transponder was read (unidentified visits, 211 rows).}
#'   \item{location}{Station (feeder) number, 101 or 102.}
#'   \item{visit_time}{Entrance time, POSIXct in UTC.}
#'   \item{duration}{Occupation time of the visit in seconds.}
#'   \item{state}{Station state code.}
#'   \item{weight}{Body weight in grams. `0` means no valid weight.}
#'   \item{feed_intake}{Feed intake of the visit in grams.}
#' }
#' @source Pig performance testing station, 2024-02-19 to 2024-05-25,
#'   30 pigs.
"nedap"

#' Example Visits from FIRE Feeding Stations
#'
#' Raw visit records exported from two FIRE (Osborne) feeding stations.
#'
#' @format A data frame with 9,794 rows and 10 columns:
#' \describe{
#'   \item{Location}{Station (feeder) number, 101 or 102.}
#'   \item{Tag}{Transponder number. `0` for unidentified visits (51 rows).}
#'   \item{Date}{Visit date, `"YYYY-MM-DD"`.}
#'   \item{Entry, Exit}{Entrance and exit clock time, `"HH:MM:SS"`. A visit
#'     that crosses midnight has `Exit < Entry` (68 rows).}
#'   \item{Ent Wt, Ext Wt}{Feed trough weight at entrance and exit, kg.}
#'   \item{Consumed}{Feed intake of the visit, kg.}
#'   \item{Weight}{Body weight, kg. `0` means no valid weight.}
#'   \item{Topup Amount}{Feed dispensed into the trough during the visit, kg.}
#' }
#' @source Pig performance testing station, 2023-12-19 to 2024-02-22,
#'   26 pigs.
"fire"
```

# Internal helpers

Small internal tools shared by every function of the package:

- **verbosity**: every exported function has `verbose = 0/1/2`
  (silent / summary / details). Messages go through `ppt_msg()`.
- **input checks**: `as_dt()` always returns a copy, so user objects are
  never modified; `check_cols()` reports missing columns.
- **per-pig fitting**: `fit_by_pig()` runs a function on each pig. A pig
  that fails is recorded and skipped instead of stopping everything.
- **removal log**: `new_removed()` builds the `removed` table returned by
  every analysis step.
- **result object**: `new_ppt_result()` gives every `calc_*()` function the
  same return structure.

```{r function-utils}
#' @filename utils
#' @import data.table
#' @importFrom cli cli_abort cli_warn
#' @importFrom utils globalVariables
#' @keywords internal
"_PACKAGE"

# ---- verbosity --------------------------------------------------------------

ppt_verbose <- function() {
  getOption("tidypptsda.verbose", 1L)
}

check_verbose <- function(verbose) {
  if (!is.numeric(verbose) || length(verbose) != 1L || is.na(verbose) ||
      !verbose %in% 0:2) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg verbose} must be 0 (silent), 1 (summary) or 2 (details).")
  }
  as.integer(verbose)
}

# Set the verbosity level until the calling function exits.
local_verbose <- function(verbose, envir = parent.frame()) {
  verbose <- check_verbose(verbose)
  # data.table's own "Processed ... groups" progress is not cli-styled and
  # cannot be silenced by verbose, so switch it off as well.
  old <- options(tidypptsda.verbose = verbose, datatable.showProgress = FALSE)
  do.call(on.exit, list(bquote(options(.(old))), add = TRUE), envir = envir)
  invisible(verbose)
}

# Print a message if the current verbosity is at least `level`.
ppt_msg <- function(msg,
                    type = c("info", "success", "warning", "danger",
                             "bullets", "h1", "h2"),
                    level = 1L,
                    .envir = parent.frame()) {
  if (ppt_verbose() < level) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  type <- match.arg(type)
  switch(type,
    info    = cli::cli_alert_info(msg, .envir = .envir),
    success = cli::cli_alert_success(msg, .envir = .envir),
    warning = cli::cli_alert_warning(msg, .envir = .envir),
    danger  = cli::cli_alert_danger(msg, .envir = .envir),
    bullets = cli::cli_bullets(msg, .envir = .envir),
    h1      = cli::cli_h1(msg, .envir = .envir),
    h2      = cli::cli_h2(msg, .envir = .envir)
  )
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Show a warning alert at the point where it happens (cli style), instead of
# an R warning that is only printed after the whole call has finished.
# Whatever triggers it is also recorded in the result (removed / flags), so
# nothing is lost when silent.
ppt_warn <- function(msg, .envir = parent.frame()) {
  if (ppt_verbose() >= 1L) {
    cli::cli_alert_warning(msg, .envir = .envir)
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

# ---- input checks -----------------------------------------------------------

# Always return a data.table that is a copy of the input.
as_dt <- function(data, arg = "data") {
  if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg {arg}} must be a data.frame or data.table, not {.cls {class(data)[1]}}.")
  }
  if (data.table::is.data.table(data)) data.table::copy(data) else data.table::as.data.table(data)
}

check_cols <- function(data, cols, arg = "data", hint = NULL) {
  missing_cols <- setdiff(cols, names(data))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "{.arg {arg}} is missing required column{?s}: {.val {missing_cols}}.",
      "i" = hint
    ))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# ---- per-pig fitting --------------------------------------------------------

# ---- parallel computing -----------------------------------------------------

check_cores <- function(cores) {
  if (!is.numeric(cores) || length(cores) != 1L || is.na(cores) || cores < 1) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg cores} must be a single number >= 1.")
  }
  max_cores <- parallel::detectCores()
  if (is.na(max_cores)) max_cores <- 1L
  as.integer(min(cores, max_cores))
}

# Set the number of cores used by fit_by_pig() until the calling function
# exits.
local_cores <- function(cores, envir = parent.frame()) {
  cores <- check_cores(cores)
  old <- options(tidypptsda.cores = cores)
  do.call(on.exit, list(bquote(options(.(old))), add = TRUE), envir = envir)
  invisible(cores)
}

# Apply `fun` to each pig. Errors are recorded in `failed` and the pig is
# skipped; warnings are recorded in `warnings` and muffled.
# `fun` must return a data.frame (or NULL to drop the pig silently).
# Pigs are processed in parallel when option tidypptsda.cores > 1.
fit_by_pig <- function(data, fun, step, by = "responder", ...) {
  groups <- split(data, by = by, keep.by = TRUE, sorted = TRUE)
  n <- length(groups)
  args <- list(...)

  one_pig <- function(g) {
    w <- character()
    res <- withCallingHandlers(
      tryCatch(do.call(fun, c(list(g), args)), error = function(e) e),
      warning = function(cnd) {
        w <<- c(w, conditionMessage(cnd))
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    )
    list(res = res, warnings = unique(w))
  }

  cores <- getOption("tidypptsda.cores", 1L)
  runs <- if (cores > 1L && n > 1L) {
    if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
      cl <- parallel::makeCluster(min(cores, n))
      on.exit(parallel::stopCluster(cl), add = TRUE)
      parallel::parLapply(cl, groups, one_pig)
    } else {
      parallel::mclapply(groups, one_pig, mc.cores = min(cores, n))
    }
  } else if (ppt_verbose() >= 1L && n > 1L) {
    # a cli progress bar; cli only draws it when the step takes > 2 s
    res <- vector("list", n)
    cli::cli_progress_bar(paste0(step, ": fitting pigs"), total = n,
                          clear = TRUE, .envir = environment())
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      res[[i]] <- one_pig(groups[[i]])
      cli::cli_progress_update(.envir = environment())
    }
    cli::cli_progress_done(.envir = environment())
    res
  } else {
    lapply(groups, one_pig)
  }

  out <- vector("list", n)
  failed <- vector("list", n)
  warns <- vector("list", n)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    id <- as.character(groups[[i]][[by]][1L])
    res <- runs[[i]]$res
    w <- runs[[i]]$warnings
    if (length(w) > 0L) {
      warns[[i]] <- data.table::data.table(responder = id, step = step, message = w)
    }
    if (inherits(res, "error")) {
      failed[[i]] <- data.table::data.table(responder = id, step = step,
                                            reason = conditionMessage(res))
      next
    }
    if (is.null(res)) next
    res <- data.table::as.data.table(res)
    if (!by %in% names(res)) {
      res[, (by) := id]
      data.table::setcolorder(res, by)
    }
    out[[i]] <- res
  }

  failed <- data.table::rbindlist(failed)
  if (nrow(failed) == 0L) {
    failed <- data.table::data.table(responder = character(), step = character(),
                                     reason = character())
  }
  warns <- data.table::rbindlist(warns)
  if (nrow(warns) == 0L) {
    warns <- data.table::data.table(responder = character(), step = character(),
                                    message = character())
  }
  list(
    result = data.table::rbindlist(out, use.names = TRUE, fill = TRUE),
    failed = failed,
    warnings = warns
  )
}

# ---- removal log ------------------------------------------------------------

# Each analysis step appends rows to this table: which pig was removed, at
# which step and why.
new_removed <- function(responder = character(), location = NA_character_,
                        step = character(), reason = character()) {
  if (length(responder) == 0L) {
    return(data.table::data.table(responder = character(), location = character(),
                                  step = character(), reason = character()))
  }
  data.table::data.table(
    responder = as.character(responder),
    location = as.character(location),
    step = as.character(step),
    reason = as.character(reason)
  )
}

# ---- result object ----------------------------------------------------------

new_ppt_result <- function(per_pig, daily, removed = new_removed(),
                           settings = list(), class) {
  structure(
    list(per_pig = per_pig, daily = daily, removed = removed,
         settings = settings),
    class = c(class, "ppt_result")
  )
}

#' @export
print.ppt_result <- function(x, ...) {
  cli::cli_h2("{.cls {class(x)[1]}}")
  pp <- x$per_pig
  if (!is.null(pp) && "status" %in% names(pp)) {
    st <- table(factor(pp$status, levels = c("keep", "low_confidence", "removed")))
    cli::cli_text("Pigs: {nrow(pp)} (keep {st[['keep']]}, low confidence {st[['low_confidence']]}, removed {st[['removed']]})")
  } else if (!is.null(pp)) {
    cli::cli_text("Pigs: {nrow(pp)}")
  }
  for (nm in setdiff(names(x), "settings")) {
    el <- x[[nm]]
    if (is.data.frame(el)) cli::cli_text("{.field ${nm}}: {nrow(el)} row{?s} x {ncol(el)} column{?s}")
  }
  cli::cli_text("QC profile: {.val {attr(x$settings, 'profile') %||% 'none'}}")
  invisible(x)
}

# ---- colours ----------------------------------------------------------------

# Okabe-Ito palette: colour-blind safe, no extra dependency.
ppt_palette <- function(n) {
  pal <- c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#E69F00",
           "#56B4E9", "#F0E442", "#000000", "#999999")
  if (n > length(pal)) {
    pal <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(pal)(n)
  }
  pal[seq_len(n)]
}
```

```{r tests-utils}
test_that("as_dt returns a copy and never modifies the input", {
  dt <- data.table::data.table(a = 1:3)
  out <- as_dt(dt)
  out[, b := 1]
  expect_false("b" %in% names(dt))
  expect_s3_class(as_dt(data.frame(a = 1)), "data.table")
  expect_error(as_dt(1:3), "data.frame")
})

test_that("check_cols names the missing columns", {
  expect_true(check_cols(data.frame(a = 1, b = 2), c("a", "b")))
  expect_error(check_cols(data.frame(a = 1), c("a", "b", "c")), "b")
})

test_that("verbosity is validated and restored on exit", {
  expect_error(check_verbose(3), "verbose")
  expect_error(check_verbose(TRUE), "verbose")
  f <- function() {
    local_verbose(0)
    ppt_verbose()
  }
  old <- getOption("tidypptsda.verbose")
  expect_equal(f(), 0L)
  expect_identical(getOption("tidypptsda.verbose"), old)
})

test_that("ppt_msg and ppt_warn respect verbose", {
  silent <- function() {
    local_verbose(0)
    ppt_msg("hidden")
    ppt_warn("hidden")
    "done"
  }
  expect_silent(silent())
  warn_now <- function() {
    local_verbose(1)
    ppt_warn("shown at once")
  }
  expect_message(warn_now(), "shown at once")
  expect_no_warning(suppressMessages(warn_now()))
  loud <- function() {
    local_verbose(1)
    ppt_msg("shown")
  }
  expect_message(loud(), "shown")
  detail <- function(v) {
    local_verbose(v)
    ppt_msg("detail only", level = 2)
  }
  expect_silent(detail(1))
  expect_message(detail(2), "detail only")
})

test_that("fit_by_pig isolates failures and records warnings", {
  dt <- data.table::data.table(responder = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), each = 3),
                               x = 1:9)
  f <- function(d) {
    if (d$responder[1] == "b") stop("too few points")
    if (d$responder[1] == "c") warning("did not converge")
    data.frame(mean_x = mean(d$x))
  }
  res <- fit_by_pig(dt, f, step = "test")
  expect_equal(res$result$responder, c("a", "c"))
  expect_equal(res$result$mean_x, c(2, 8))
  expect_equal(res$failed$responder, "b")
  expect_match(res$failed$reason, "too few points")
  expect_equal(res$warnings$responder, "c")
  expect_match(res$warnings$message, "converge")
  # no failures: empty tables keep their columns
  ok <- fit_by_pig(dt[responder == "a"], f, step = "test")
  expect_named(ok$failed, c("responder", "step", "reason"))
  expect_named(ok$warnings, c("responder", "step", "message"))
})

test_that("new_removed builds a consistent log", {
  empty <- new_removed()
  expect_equal(nrow(empty), 0L)
  expect_named(empty, c("responder", "location", "step", "reason"))
  log <- new_removed(c(1, 2), "101", "weight_range", "too light")
  expect_type(log$responder, "character")
  expect_equal(nrow(log), 2L)
})

test_that("ppt_palette returns n colours", {
  expect_length(ppt_palette(3), 3L)
  expect_length(ppt_palette(15), 15L)
})
```

# qc_config

All quality-control thresholds live in one object created by `qc_config()`.
Three presets are available, and any single parameter can be overridden.

```{r function-qc_config}
#' Build Quality-Control Settings from a Preset
#'
#' @description
#' Build the set of quality-control (QC) thresholds used by the whole
#' pipeline. Start from a preset with `profile` and override any parameter
#' through `...`.
#'
#' @param profile Preset to start from:
#'   - `"casey"` (default): feeder error criteria of Casey et al. (2005),
#'     robust regression (`MASS::rlm`) for body weight outliers and a
#'     quadratic growth curve.
#'   - `"national"`: LOESS-based weight cleaning and growth curve, a
#'     minimum curve R², longer test period and lower missing rate.
#'   - `"legacy"`: STL + robust regression + robust SD outlier detection
#'     and a Gompertz growth curve.
#' @param ... Parameters to override, as `name = value`. See **Parameters**.
#'
#' @section Parameters:
#' **Station transfer** (pigs seen at several stations)
#' - `max_gap_days`: maximum gap between two stations to treat the pig as
#'   transferred. A larger gap splits it into two animals. Default 3.
#' - `max_overlap_days`: maximum time overlap between two stations. A larger
#'   overlap is treated as transponder misreads. Default 1.
#' - `max_jump_kg`: body weight jump at the transfer that triggers a
#'   warning. Default 10.
#'
#' **Body weight records**
#' - `weight_range`: valid body weight of a single record, kg.
#' - `weight_outlier`: one or more of `"rlm"`, `"loess"`, `"stl"`, `"sd"`.
#' - `outlier_combine`: `"any"` (outlier for any method) or `"majority"`.
#' - `rlm_cutoff`: records with a robust regression weight below this are
#'   outliers. Default 0.5.
#' - `sd_max`: residuals beyond this many robust SDs (MAD) are outliers.
#' - `loess_span`: smoothing span for LOESS. Default 0.75.
#' - `rel_dev_max`: optional, relative deviation from the curve above which
#'   a record is an outlier (e.g. 0.25). `NULL` = off.
#' - `daily_drop_min`: optional, a day whose weight is below this ratio of
#'   the previous day is an outlier (e.g. 0.90). `NULL` = off.
#'
#' **Pig-level checks**
#' - `min_test_days`, `min_records`: minimum test length (days) and number
#'   of valid weight records.
#' - `max_missing_rate`: maximum share of days without a valid weight.
#' - `entry_weight_max`, `exit_weight_min`: maximum entry and minimum exit
#'   body weight, kg.
#' - `curve_r2_min`: optional, pigs whose growth curve R² is below this are
#'   flagged as low confidence (not removed). `NULL` = off.
#' - `max_daily_jump_kg`: optional, pigs whose daily median weight changes
#'   by more than this many kg per day between consecutive days are flagged
#'   as low confidence (not removed). `NULL` = off.
#'
#' **Growth and ADG**
#' - `stage_range`: body weight interval for ADG and FCR, kg.
#' - `curve_model`: `"poly1"`, `"poly2"`, `"poly3"`, `"loess"` or
#'   `"gompertz"` (falls back to `"poly2"` when it does not converge).
#' - `max_extrap_days`: maximum extrapolation of the curve, days.
#'
#' **Feeder errors** (Casey et al. 2005, Table 3)
#' - `fiv_range`: FIV-lo / FIV-hi, feed intake per visit, g.
#' - `fiv0_abs_max`: FIV-0, maximum |FIV| for a 0 s visit, g.
#' - `duration_max`: OTV-hi, maximum occupation time per visit, s.
#' - `speed_fiv_lo_max`: FRV-hi-FIV-lo, maximum feeding rate for visits with
#'   0 < FIV < 50 g, g/min.
#' - `speed_strict_max`: FRV-hi-strict, maximum feeding rate when the
#'   preceding or following visit has FIV < -20 g, g/min.
#' - `speed_range`: FRV-lo and FRV-hi, g/min.
#' - `idle_duration_max`: FRV-0, maximum occupation time with no intake, s.
#' - `trough_diff_range`: LWD / FWD, trough weight difference between
#'   subsequent visits, g.
#' - `max_unidentified_feed_kg`: feed disappearance in unidentified visits
#'   per feeder above which a warning is given.
#' - `fiv_max_by_weight`: optional table that replaces the upper limit of
#'   `fiv_range` (FIV-hi) by a limit that depends on body weight, and
#'   optionally on breed. Columns `weight_from` (kg, lower bound of the
#'   weight class), `fiv_max` (g) and optionally `breed`. See
#'   [fiv_max_example()]. `NULL` = off.
#'
#' **Daily feed intake**
#' - `dfi_range`: valid daily feed intake, kg.
#' - `dfi_quantile`: optional, lower and upper quantile cut-offs (e.g.
#'   `c(0.025, 0.99)`). `NULL` = off.
#' - `dfi_correct`: `"lmm"` (Jiao et al. 2014) or `"none"`.
#' - `impute_method`: `"linear"` (linear interpolation, LOESS for long
#'   gaps, intake ~ body weight regression at the stage ends) or `"loess"`
#'   (robust LOESS over days everywhere).
#' - `long_gap_days`: inside gaps longer than this many days are imputed
#'   with LOESS instead of a straight line (`impute_method = "linear"`).
#'   Default 7.
#'
#' **Confidence flags** (used by [calc_fcr()])
#' - `max_edge_extrap_days`: a pig is `"low_confidence"` when the growth
#'   curve or the feed intake is extrapolated over more than this many days
#'   at the start or the end of the stage. Default 15.
#' - `min_coverage`: minimum share of stage days with recorded feed intake.
#'   Default 0.7.
#' - `bin_width`: width of the body weight classes used for the segment
#'   checks of [calc_fcr()], kg. Default 10.
#' - `min_bin_coverage_kg`: an inner weight class whose recorded body
#'   weights span less than this many kg flags the pig. Default 6.
#' - `bin_fcr_limits`: optional table of plausible FCR per weight class,
#'   columns `weight_from` (kg), `fcr_min`, `fcr_max`. See
#'   [bin_fcr_example()]. `NULL` = off.
#'
#' @return An object of class `ppt_qc`: a named list of parameters with the
#'   preset name in attribute `"profile"`.
#'
#' @references
#' Casey, D. S., Stern, H. S., & Dekkers, J. C. M. (2005). Identification of
#' errors and factors associated with errors in data from electronic swine
#' feeders. *Journal of Animal Science*, 83, 969-982.
#'
#' Jiao, S., Maltecca, C., Gray, K. A., & Cassady, J. P. (2014). Feed intake,
#' average daily gain, feed efficiency, and real-time ultrasound traits in
#' Duroc pigs: I. *Journal of Animal Science*, 92, 2377-2386.
#'
#' @filename qc_config
#' @export
qc_config <- function(profile = c("casey", "national", "legacy"), ...) {
  if (!is.character(profile)) {
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "{.arg profile} must be one of {.val {c('casey', 'national', 'legacy')}}.",
      "i" = "Parameters to override must be named, e.g. {.code qc_config(\"casey\", duration_max = 1800)}."
    ))
  }
  profile <- match.arg(profile)
  cfg <- qc_defaults()
  cfg <- qc_set(cfg, qc_presets()[[profile]])

  overrides <- list(...)
  if (length(overrides) > 0L) {
    nms <- names(overrides)
    if (is.null(nms) || any(!nzchar(nms))) {
      cli::cli_abort("All parameters in {.arg ...} must be named.")
    }
    unknown <- setdiff(nms, names(cfg))
    if (length(unknown) > 0L) {
      hints <- vapply(unknown, function(u) {
        m <- agrep(u, names(cfg), max.distance = 0.3, value = TRUE)
        if (length(m) > 0L) paste0("did you mean {.val ", m[1L], "}?") else ""
      }, character(1))
      cli::cli_abort(c(
        "Unknown QC parameter{?s}: {.val {unknown}}.",
        stats::setNames(hints[nzchar(hints)], rep("i", sum(nzchar(hints))))
      ))
    }
    cfg <- qc_set(cfg, overrides)
  }

  qc_validate(cfg)
  structure(cfg, profile = profile, class = "ppt_qc")
}

#' @export
print.ppt_qc <- function(x, ...) {
  cli::cli_h2("QC settings: profile {.val {attr(x, 'profile')}}")
  groups <- qc_groups()
  fmt <- function(v) {
    if (is.null(v)) return("NULL (off)")
    if (is.data.frame(v)) return(sprintf("table (%d rows)", nrow(v)))
    paste(format(v), collapse = ", ")
  }
  for (g in unique(groups)) {
    cli::cli_text("{.strong {g}}")
    nms <- names(groups)[groups == g]
    lines <- vapply(nms, function(nm) paste0("{.field ", nm, "}: ", fmt(x[[nm]])), character(1))
    cli::cli_bullets(stats::setNames(lines, rep(" ", length(lines))))
  }
  invisible(x)
}

#' Example threshold tables
#'
#' @description
#' Example tables for the optional QC parameters `fiv_max_by_weight` and
#' `bin_fcr_limits` of [qc_config()].
#'
#' - `fiv_max_example()`: maximum feed intake per visit (g) by breed
#'   (`"YY"`, `"LL"`, `"DD"`) and 10 kg body weight class from 20 to 140 kg.
#' - `bin_fcr_example()`: plausible feed conversion ratio per 10 kg body
#'   weight class from 30 to 120 kg.
#'
#' The values come from in-house quality-control scripts of a pig testing
#' station, not from the literature. Check them against your own data
#' before use.
#'
#' @return A `data.table`. `fiv_max_example()`: `breed`, `weight_from`
#'   (kg), `fiv_max` (g). `bin_fcr_example()`: `weight_from` (kg),
#'   `fcr_min`, `fcr_max`.
#' @export
#' @examples
#' fiv_max_example()
#' qc <- qc_config(fiv_max_by_weight = fiv_max_example(),
#'                 bin_fcr_limits = bin_fcr_example())
fiv_max_example <- function() {
  w <- seq(20, 130, by = 10)
  data.table::data.table(

                821.6, 1044.8, 1268.0, 1491.2, 1714.4, 1937.7, 2160.9, 2384.1, 2607.3, 2830.5, 3053.7, 3277.0,
                712.6, 916.9, 1121.2, 1325.4, 1529.7, 1734.0, 1938.2, 2142.5, 2346.8, 2551.0, 2755.3, 2959.6)
  )
}

#' @rdname fiv_max_example
#' @export
bin_fcr_example <- function() {

# Assign values one by one so that NULL values are kept, not dropped.
qc_set <- function(cfg, values) {
  for (nm in names(values)) {
    cfg[nm] <- list(values[[nm]])
  }
  cfg
}

# Validation rules for each parameter.
qc_spec <- function() {
  num <- function(min = -Inf, max = Inf, null = FALSE) list(type = "num", min = min, max = max, null = null)
  rng <- function(min = -Inf, max = Inf, null = FALSE) list(type = "range", min = min, max = max, null = null)
  chc <- function(choices, multiple = FALSE) list(type = "choice", choices = choices, multiple = multiple, null = FALSE)
  tbl <- function(cols, optional = character()) list(type = "table", cols = cols, optional = optional, null = TRUE)
  list(
    max_gap_days = num(0), max_overlap_days = num(0), max_jump_kg = num(0),
    weight_range = rng(0), weight_outlier = chc(c("rlm", "loess", "stl", "sd"), multiple = TRUE),
    outlier_combine = chc(c("any", "majority")),
    rlm_cutoff = num(0, 1), sd_max = num(0), loess_span = num(0.1, 1),
    rel_dev_max = num(0, 1, null = TRUE), daily_drop_min = num(0, 1, null = TRUE),
    min_test_days = num(1), min_records = num(3), max_missing_rate = num(0, 1),
    entry_weight_max = num(0), exit_weight_min = num(0),
    curve_r2_min = num(0, 1, null = TRUE), max_daily_jump_kg = num(0, null = TRUE),
    stage_range = rng(0), curve_model = chc(c("poly1", "poly2", "poly3", "loess", "gompertz")),
    max_extrap_days = num(0),
    fiv_range = rng(), fiv0_abs_max = num(0), duration_max = num(0),
    speed_fiv_lo_max = num(0), speed_strict_max = num(0), speed_range = rng(0),
    idle_duration_max = num(0), trough_diff_range = rng(),
    max_unidentified_feed_kg = num(0),
    fiv_max_by_weight = tbl(c("weight_from", "fiv_max"), optional = "breed"),
    dfi_range = rng(0), dfi_quantile = rng(0, 1, null = TRUE),
    dfi_correct = chc(c("lmm", "none")),
    impute_method = chc(c("linear", "loess")),
    long_gap_days = num(1),
    max_edge_extrap_days = num(0), min_coverage = num(0, 1),
    bin_width = num(1), min_bin_coverage_kg = num(0),
    bin_fcr_limits = tbl(c("weight_from", "fcr_min", "fcr_max"))
  )
}

qc_validate <- function(cfg) {
  spec <- qc_spec()
  for (nm in names(spec)) {
    s <- spec[[nm]]
    v <- cfg[[nm]]
    if (is.null(v)) {
      if (!s$null) cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} cannot be NULL.")
      next
    }
    if (s$type == "num") {
      if (!is.numeric(v) || length(v) != 1L || is.na(v) || v < s$min || v > s$max) {
        cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} must be a single number between {s$min} and {s$max}, not {.val {v}}.")
      }
    } else if (s$type == "range") {
      if (!is.numeric(v) || length(v) != 2L || anyNA(v) || v[1L] >= v[2L] ||
          any(v < s$min) || any(v > s$max)) {
        cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} must be two increasing numbers between {s$min} and {s$max}, not {.val {v}}.")
      }
    } else if (s$type == "table") {
      check_qc_table(v, nm, s$cols, s$optional)
    } else if (s$type == "choice") {
      ok <- is.character(v) && length(v) >= 1L && all(v %in% s$choices) &&
        (s$multiple || length(v) == 1L) && !anyDuplicated(v)
      if (!ok) {
        cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} must be {if (s$multiple) 'one or more of' else 'one of'} {.val {s$choices}}, not {.val {v}}.")
      }
    }
  }

  # Cross-parameter consistency
  if (cfg$stage_range[1L] < cfg$weight_range[1L] || cfg$stage_range[2L] > cfg$weight_range[2L]) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.field stage_range} ({cfg$stage_range[1]}-{cfg$stage_range[2]} kg) must lie inside {.field weight_range} ({cfg$weight_range[1]}-{cfg$weight_range[2]} kg).")
  }
  if (cfg$entry_weight_max >= cfg$exit_weight_min) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.field entry_weight_max} must be smaller than {.field exit_weight_min}.")
  }
  if (cfg$outlier_combine == "majority" && length(cfg$weight_outlier) < 2L) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.field outlier_combine = \"majority\"} needs at least two methods in {.field weight_outlier}.")
  }
  if (cfg$min_bin_coverage_kg > cfg$bin_width) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.field min_bin_coverage_kg} cannot be larger than {.field bin_width}.")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Table parameters: required numeric columns, optional character columns,
# one row per (optional key, weight_from).
check_qc_table <- function(v, nm, cols, optional) {
  if (!is.data.frame(v)) {
    cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} must be a data frame with columns {.val {cols}}.")
  }
  miss <- setdiff(cols, names(v))
  if (length(miss) > 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} is missing column{?s} {.val {miss}}.")
  }
  for (cl in cols) {
    if (!is.numeric(v[[cl]]) || anyNA(v[[cl]])) {
      cli::cli_abort("Column {.field {cl}} of {.field {nm}} must be numeric without NA.")
    }
  }
  if (nrow(v) == 0L) cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} has no rows.")
  keys <- intersect(optional, names(v))
  key <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(c(keys, "weight_from"), function(k) v[[k]]), sep = "|"))
  if (anyDuplicated(key)) {
    cli::cli_abort("QC parameter {.field {nm}} has duplicated {.field weight_from} rows{if (length(keys)) ' within a breed' else ''}.")
  }
  if (all(c("fcr_min", "fcr_max") %in% names(v)) && any(v$fcr_min >= v$fcr_max)) {
    cli::cli_abort("In {.field {nm}}, {.field fcr_min} must be smaller than {.field fcr_max}.")
  }
  if ("fiv_max" %in% names(v) && any(v$fiv_max <= 0)) {
    cli::cli_abort("In {.field {nm}}, {.field fiv_max} must be positive.")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

```{r example-qc_config}
# Default preset
qc <- qc_config()
qc$duration_max

# Another preset with one parameter overridden
qc_national <- qc_config("national", min_test_days = 50)
qc_national

# Optional rules are off (NULL) unless switched on
qc_config("casey", daily_drop_min = 0.90)$daily_drop_min
```

```{r tests-qc_config}
test_that("all presets are valid and differ where documented", {
  casey <- qc_config()
  national <- qc_config("national")
  legacy <- qc_config("legacy")
  for (q in list(casey, national, legacy)) {
    expect_s3_class(q, "ppt_qc")
    expect_setequal(names(q), names(qc_defaults()))
  }
  expect_equal(attr(casey, "profile"), "casey")
  expect_equal(casey$duration_max, 3600)
  expect_equal(casey$speed_range, c(2, 170))
  expect_null(casey$rel_dev_max)
  expect_equal(national$weight_range, c(25, 140))
  expect_equal(national$impute_method, "loess")
  expect_equal(casey$max_edge_extrap_days, 15)
  expect_error(qc_config(impute_method = "cumulative_loess"), "impute_method")
  expect_equal(legacy$stage_range, c(45, 110))
  expect_equal(legacy$weight_outlier, c("stl", "rlm", "sd"))
})

test_that("overrides apply on top of the preset", {
  q <- qc_config("national", min_test_days = 50, daily_drop_min = 0.9)
  expect_equal(q$min_test_days, 50)
  expect_equal(q$daily_drop_min, 0.9)
  expect_equal(q$max_missing_rate, 0.15)
  # NULL switches an optional rule off
  expect_null(qc_config("national", curve_r2_min = NULL)$curve_r2_min)
  expect_true("curve_r2_min" %in% names(qc_config("national", curve_r2_min = NULL)))
})

test_that("unknown or unnamed parameters are rejected", {
  expect_error(qc_config(duration = 1800), "duration_max")
  expect_error(qc_config("casey", 1800), "named")
  expect_error(qc_config(1800), "profile")
  expect_error(qc_config("other"))
})

test_that("invalid values are rejected", {
  expect_error(qc_config(duration_max = -1), "duration_max")
  expect_error(qc_config(duration_max = "1800"), "duration_max")
  expect_error(qc_config(weight_range = c(140, 25)), "weight_range")
  expect_error(qc_config(curve_model = "spline"), "curve_model")
  expect_error(qc_config(weight_outlier = c("rlm", "rlm")), "weight_outlier")
  expect_error(qc_config(rlm_cutoff = NULL), "NULL")
})

test_that("table parameters are validated", {
  expect_silent(qc_config(fiv_max_by_weight = fiv_max_example(),
                          bin_fcr_limits = bin_fcr_example()))
  expect_error(qc_config(fiv_max_by_weight = data.frame(weight_from = 20)), "fiv_max")
  expect_error(qc_config(fiv_max_by_weight = data.frame(weight_from = c(20, 20), fiv_max = 1:2)), "duplicated")
  expect_silent(qc_config(fiv_max_by_weight = data.frame(breed = c("A", "B"), weight_from = c(20, 20), fiv_max = 1:2)))
  expect_error(qc_config(bin_fcr_limits = data.frame(weight_from = 30, fcr_min = 3, fcr_max = 2)), "fcr_min")
  expect_error(qc_config(bin_fcr_limits = "x"), "data frame")
  expect_error(qc_config(min_bin_coverage_kg = 12), "bin_width")
  expect_message(print(qc_config(bin_fcr_limits = bin_fcr_example())), "table")
  expect_equal(nrow(fiv_max_example()), 36L)
})

test_that("cross-parameter checks work", {
  expect_error(qc_config(stage_range = c(10, 120)), "stage_range")
  expect_error(qc_config(entry_weight_max = 90), "entry_weight_max")
  expect_error(qc_config(outlier_combine = "majority"), "majority")
  expect_silent(qc_config("legacy", outlier_combine = "majority"))
})

test_that("print method runs", {
  expect_message(print(qc_config("legacy")), "legacy")
})
```

# read_station

`read_station()` reads one or many station export files (or a whole
folder) and stacks them into one table. Columns are checked against the
station type, transponder IDs are always read as text so leading zeros are
kept, and a `source_file` column records where each row came from.

```{r function-read_station}
#' Read Feeding Station Export Files
#'
#' @description
#' Read one or more CSV exports from NEDAP or FIRE feeding stations and
#' combine them into one table.
#'
#' @param files Character vector of file paths, or a single folder. For a
#'   folder, all files matching `pattern` are read.
#' @param station `"nedap"`, `"fire"` or `NULL` (default) to detect the
#'   station type from the column names.
#' @param pattern Regular expression for file names when `files` is a
#'   folder. Default `"\\.csv$"` (case-insensitive).
#' @param fill If `FALSE` (default), all files must have the same columns.
#'   If `TRUE`, missing columns are filled with `NA`.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details per file).
#' @param ... Further arguments passed to [data.table::fread()].
#'
#' @return A `data.table` with the original columns plus `source_file`
#'   (file name without folder). Its attribute `"station"` holds the station
#'   type.
#'
#' @details
#' Required columns:
#' - NEDAP: `responder`, `location`, `visit_time`, `duration`, `weight`,
#'   `feed_intake`.
#' - FIRE: `Location`, `Tag`, `Date`, `Entry`, `Exit`, `Ent Wt`, `Ext Wt`,
#'   `Consumed`, `Weight`.
#'
#' Transponder and animal ID columns (`responder`, `animal_number`,
#' `lifenumber`, `Tag`) are read as character.
#'
#' @export
read_station <- function(files,
                         station = NULL,
                         pattern = "\\.csv$",
                         fill = FALSE,
                         verbose = 1,
                         ...) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  files <- resolve_files(files, pattern)
  if (!is.null(station)) station <- check_station(station)

  ppt_msg("Reading {length(files)} file{?s}", "h1")

  tables <- lapply(files, function(f) {
    header <- names(data.table::fread(f, nrows = 0L, showProgress = FALSE, ...))
    ids <- intersect(id_cols(), header)
    cc <- if (length(ids) > 0L) list(character = ids) else NULL
    dt <- data.table::fread(f, colClasses = cc, showProgress = FALSE, ...)
    ppt_msg("{.file {basename(f)}}: {nrow(dt)} rows, {ncol(dt)} columns",
            "info", level = 2)
    dt
  })
  names(tables) <- basename(files)

  # Station type: detect from the first file, then require it everywhere.
  if (is.null(station)) {
    station <- detect_station(tables[[1L]])
    ppt_msg("Detected station type {.val {station}}", "info")
  }
  required <- station_cols(station)
  for (nm in names(tables)) {
    check_cols(tables[[nm]], required, arg = nm,
               hint = paste0("Is station = \"", station, "\" correct?"))
  }

  # Same columns in every file, unless fill = TRUE.
  col_sets <- lapply(tables, names)
  all_cols <- unique(unlist(col_sets))
  differ <- vapply(col_sets, function(x) !setequal(x, all_cols), logical(1))
  if (any(differ) && !fill) {
    details <- vapply(names(tables)[differ], function(nm) {
      paste0(nm, " lacks: ", paste(setdiff(all_cols, col_sets[[nm]]), collapse = ", "))
    }, character(1))
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "Files do not have the same columns.",
      stats::setNames(details, rep("x", length(details))),
      "i" = "Use {.code fill = TRUE} to fill missing columns with {.val NA}."
    ))
  }

  out <- data.table::rbindlist(tables, use.names = TRUE, fill = fill,
                               idcol = "source_file")
  data.table::setcolorder(out, setdiff(names(out), "source_file"))
  data.table::setattr(out, "station", station)

  ppt_msg("Read {nrow(out)} rows from {length(files)} file{?s} ({toupper(station)})",
          "success")
  out
}

# Columns read as character so that leading zeros in IDs are kept.
id_cols <- function() {
  c("responder", "animal_number", "lifenumber", "Tag")
}

station_cols <- function(station) {
  switch(station,
    nedap = c("responder", "location", "visit_time", "duration",
              "weight", "feed_intake"),
    fire = c("Location", "Tag", "Date", "Entry", "Exit",
             "Ent Wt", "Ext Wt", "Consumed", "Weight")
  )
}

check_station <- function(station) {
  if (!is.character(station) || length(station) != 1L ||
      !tolower(station) %in% c("nedap", "fire")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg station} must be {.val nedap} or {.val fire}, not {.val {station}}.")
  }
  tolower(station)
}

detect_station <- function(data) {
  is_nedap <- all(station_cols("nedap") %in% names(data))
  is_fire <- all(station_cols("fire") %in% names(data))
  if (is_nedap && !is_fire) return("nedap")
  if (is_fire && !is_nedap) return("fire")
  cli::cli_abort(c(
    "Cannot detect the station type from the column names.",
    "i" = "NEDAP needs: {.val {station_cols('nedap')}}.",
    "i" = "FIRE needs: {.val {station_cols('fire')}}.",
    "i" = "Set {.arg station} explicitly."
  ))
}

resolve_files <- function(files, pattern) {
  if (!is.character(files) || length(files) == 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg files} must be file paths or a folder.")
  }
  if (length(files) == 1L && dir.exists(files)) {
    folder <- files
    files <- list.files(folder, pattern = pattern, full.names = TRUE,
                        ignore.case = TRUE)
    if (length(files) == 0L) {
      cli::cli_abort("No files matching {.val {pattern}} in {.path {folder}}.")
    }
    return(sort(files))
  }
  missing_files <- files[!file.exists(files)]
  if (length(missing_files) > 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort("File{?s} not found: {.path {missing_files}}.")
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(basename(files))) {
    cli::cli_abort("File names must be unique: {.val {basename(files)[duplicated(basename(files))]}}.")
  }
  files
}
```

```{r example-read_station}
data.table::fwrite(fire[fire$Location == 102, ], file.path(folder, "fire_102.csv"))

raw <- read_station(folder)

attr(raw, "station")

unlink(folder, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r tests-read_station}
write_split <- function(data, by, folder) {
  dir.create(folder, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (v in unique(data[[by]])) {
    data.table::fwrite(data[data[[by]] == v, ], file.path(folder, paste0("part_", v, ".csv")))
  }
  sort(list.files(folder, full.names = TRUE))
}

test_that("multiple FIRE files are combined and the station is detected", {
  folder <- withr::local_tempdir()
  files <- write_split(fire, "Location", folder)
  out <- read_station(files, verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(nrow(out), nrow(fire))
  expect_equal(attr(out, "station"), "fire")
  expect_equal(sort(unique(out$source_file)), c("part_101.csv", "part_102.csv"))
  expect_type(out$Tag, "character")
  # a folder gives the same result
  expect_equal(nrow(read_station(folder, verbose = 0)), nrow(fire))
})

test_that("NEDAP files keep IDs as text, including leading zeros", {

  nd <- nedap[!is.na(nedap$responder), ]
  nd$responder <- formatC(nd$responder, width = 6, flag = "0")

test_that("column mismatches are reported, or filled when asked", {

})

test_that("wrong inputs give clear errors", {

  expect_error(read_station(file.path(folder, "nope.csv")), "not found")

  expect_error(read_station(folder, station = "other"), "nedap")

  data.table::fwrite(data.frame(x = 1), bad)

})
```

# prep_visits

`prep_visits()` turns a raw NEDAP or FIRE export into one standard visit
table that every later step uses:

- one row per visit, **including unidentified visits** (no transponder
  read), marked with `identified = FALSE`. They are needed to compute the
  differences between subsequent visits on a feeder (Casey et al. 2005);
- the same column names and units for both stations: body weight in kg,
  feed intake and trough weights in g, times as POSIXct (UTC);
- FIRE visits that cross midnight get the right exit time;
- a body weight of 0 becomes `NA`;
- pigs seen at more than one station are kept (see **Station transfer**).

```{r function-prep_visits}
#' Prepare a Standard Visit Table
#'
#' @description
#' Convert raw NEDAP or FIRE station data into a standard visit table with
#' the same columns and units for both station types.
#'
#' @param data Raw station data, e.g. from [read_station()] or the example
#'   datasets [nedap] and [fire].
#' @param station `"nedap"`, `"fire"` or `NULL` (default): taken from the
#'   `"station"` attribute set by [read_station()], or detected from the
#'   column names.
#' @param qc QC settings from [qc_config()]. Used here: `duration_max` (to
#'   tell a FIRE midnight crossing from a recording error) and the station
#'   transfer parameters `max_gap_days`, `max_overlap_days`, `max_jump_kg`.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details).
#'
#' @return A `data.table`, one row per visit, ordered by `location` and
#'   `entry_time`:
#'   - `responder`: pig ID (character, `NA` for unidentified visits);
#'     `responder_raw`: transponder number as recorded;
#'   - `breed`: kept when the input has a `breed` column; otherwise add it
#'     with [add_breed()];
#'   - `identified`: `FALSE` for visits without a transponder read;
#'   - `location`: station (feeder) ID, character;
#'   - `date`, `seq_days` (day number from the first day in the data, 1 =
#'     first day), `seq_in_day` (visit number of the pig that day),
#'     `seq_in_location` (visit number on the feeder that day);
#'   - `entry_time`, `exit_time`: POSIXct, UTC; `duration`: seconds;
#'   - `feed_intake`: g; `weight`: body weight, kg (`NA` if not recorded);
#'   - `trough_in`, `trough_out`: trough weight at entrance and exit, g
#'     (FIRE only, `NA` for NEDAP); `topup`: feed dispensed, g (FIRE only);
#'   - `source_file`, if present in the input.
#'
#'   Attributes:
#'   - `"station"`: station type;
#'   - `"stations"`: one row per pig with its station history (see below);
#'   - `"removed"`: log of visits removed as transponder misreads;
#'   - `"prep_summary"`: number of rows dropped at each step.
#'
#' @section Station transfer:
#' For each pig seen at several stations, the time span at each station is
#' compared:
#' - **misread**: the span at a minor station overlaps the span at the main
#'   station (most visits) by more than `max_overlap_days`. Visits at the
#'   minor station inside the main span are removed as transponder misreads.
#' - **transfer**: consecutive spans are separated by at most
#'   `max_gap_days`. All visits are kept, each with its real `location`. A
#'   body weight jump above `max_jump_kg` at the transfer gives a warning.
#' - **split**: a gap longer than `max_gap_days`. The spans are treated as
#'   different animals and `responder` becomes `"<id>_<location>"`.
#'
#' A pig that returns to a station it already used is not supported: the
#' return looks like an overlap and is treated as misreads.
#'
#' @seealso [read_station()] for the previous step.
#' @export
prep_visits <- function(data, station = NULL, qc = qc_config(), verbose = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  if (!inherits(qc, "ppt_qc")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg qc} must be created with {.fn qc_config}.")
  }
  if (is.null(station)) station <- attr(data, "station", exact = TRUE)
  dt <- as_dt(data)
  station <- if (is.null(station)) detect_station(dt) else check_station(station)
  check_cols(dt, station_cols(station))

  ppt_msg("Preparing {toupper(station)} visits", "h1")
  n_raw <- nrow(dt)

  dt <- switch(station,
    nedap = standardise_nedap(dt),
    fire = standardise_fire(dt, qc$duration_max)
  )
  n_cross <- attr(dt, "n_midnight")

  # Body weight of 0 (or below) means no weight was recorded.
  n_zero_weight <- dt[!is.na(weight) & weight <= 0, .N]
  dt[weight <= 0, weight := NA_real_]

  # Rows without an entry time cannot be placed in the feeder sequence.
  n_no_time <- dt[is.na(entry_time), .N]
  dt <- dt[!is.na(entry_time)]

  # Exact duplicate visits.
  n_before <- nrow(dt)
  dt <- unique(dt)
  n_dup <- n_before - nrow(dt)

  ppt_bullets_counts(c(
    "Visits read" = n_raw,
    "Unidentified visits (kept, identified = FALSE)" = dt[identified == FALSE, .N],
    "FIRE visits crossing midnight (exit time corrected)" = if (station == "fire") n_cross else NA,
    "Body weights of 0 set to NA" = n_zero_weight,
    "Rows without entry time (dropped)" = n_no_time,
    "Duplicated rows (dropped)" = n_dup
  ))

  # Pigs seen at more than one station.
  tr <- resolve_transfers(dt, qc)
  dt <- tr$visits

  # Sequence numbers.
  data.table::setorder(dt, location, entry_time)
  dt[, date := as.Date(entry_time, tz = "UTC")]
  dt[, seq_days := as.integer(date - min(date)) + 1L]
  dt[, seq_in_location := seq_len(.N), by = .(location, date)]
  dt[identified == TRUE, seq_in_day := seq_len(.N), by = .(responder, date)]

  cols <- c("responder", "responder_raw", "identified", "breed", "location",
            "date", "seq_days", "seq_in_day", "seq_in_location", "entry_time",
            "exit_time", "duration", "feed_intake", "weight", "trough_in",
            "trough_out", "topup", "source_file")
  cols <- intersect(cols, names(dt))
  dt <- dt[, cols, with = FALSE]

  data.table::setattr(dt, "station", station)
  data.table::setattr(dt, "stations", tr$stations)
  data.table::setattr(dt, "removed", tr$removed)
  data.table::setattr(dt, "prep_summary", list(
    rows_read = n_raw, midnight_crossings = n_cross,
    zero_weights = n_zero_weight, no_entry_time = n_no_time,
    duplicates = n_dup, misreads = nrow(tr$misread_visits)
  ))

  ppt_msg("{data.table::uniqueN(dt$responder, na.rm = TRUE)} pigs at {data.table::uniqueN(dt$location)} station{?s}, {nrow(dt)} visits over {max(dt$seq_days)} days", "success")
  if (!"breed" %in% names(dt)) {
    ppt_msg("No {.field breed} column. To use breed in the feed intake model and breed-specific limits, add it with {.fn add_breed}.", "info")
  }
  dt
}

standardise_nedap <- function(dt) {
  if (!inherits(dt$visit_time, "POSIXct")) {
    dt[, visit_time := as.POSIXct(as.character(visit_time), tz = "UTC")]
  }
  # NEDAP exports body weight in g; accept kg if the values are clearly kg.
  w <- dt$weight[!is.na(dt$weight) & dt$weight > 0]
  weight_div <- if (length(w) > 0L && stats::median(w) < 1000) 1 else 1000
  out <- dt[, .(
    responder_raw = as.character(responder),
    location = as.character(location),
    entry_time = visit_time,
    duration = as.numeric(duration),
    feed_intake = as.numeric(feed_intake),
    weight = as.numeric(weight) / weight_div,
    trough_in = NA_real_,
    trough_out = NA_real_,
    topup = NA_real_
  )]
  if ("source_file" %in% names(dt)) out[, source_file := dt$source_file]
  if ("breed" %in% names(dt)) out[, breed := as.character(dt$breed)]
  out[, exit_time := entry_time + duration]
  finish_ids(out)
  data.table::setattr(out, "n_midnight", 0L)
  out
}

standardise_fire <- function(dt, duration_max) {
  day <- as.character(dt$Date)
  entry <- as.POSIXct(paste(day, dt$Entry), tz = "UTC")
  exit <- as.POSIXct(paste(day, dt$Exit), tz = "UTC")
  # FIRE stores clock times only. An exit before the entry is a midnight
  # crossing when the corrected duration is plausible; otherwise it stays
  # negative and is caught later as error OTV-lo.
  crossing <- !is.na(exit) & !is.na(entry) & exit < entry &
    as.numeric(difftime(exit + 86400, entry, units = "secs")) <= duration_max
  exit[crossing] <- exit[crossing] + 86400

  out <- data.table::data.table(
    responder_raw = as.character(dt$Tag),
    location = as.character(dt$Location),
    entry_time = entry,
    exit_time = exit,
    duration = as.numeric(difftime(exit, entry, units = "secs")),
    feed_intake = as.numeric(dt$Consumed) * 1000,
    weight = as.numeric(dt$Weight),
    trough_in = as.numeric(dt$`Ent Wt`) * 1000,
    trough_out = as.numeric(dt$`Ext Wt`) * 1000,
    topup = if ("Topup Amount" %in% names(dt)) as.numeric(dt$`Topup Amount`) * 1000 else NA_real_
  )
  if ("source_file" %in% names(dt)) out[, source_file := dt$source_file]
  if ("breed" %in% names(dt)) out[, breed := as.character(dt$breed)]
  finish_ids(out)
  data.table::setattr(out, "n_midnight", sum(crossing))
  out
}

# Transponder 0, empty or NA means the visit was not identified.
finish_ids <- function(out) {
  raw <- trimws(out$responder_raw)
  unidentified <- is.na(raw) | raw == "" | suppressWarnings(as.numeric(raw)) %in% 0
  out[, identified := !unidentified]
  out[, responder := data.table::fifelse(identified, raw, NA_character_)]
  invisible(out)
}

ppt_bullets_counts <- function(counts, level = 1L) {
  counts <- counts[!is.na(counts)]
  lines <- paste0(names(counts), ": {.strong ", format(counts, big.mark = ","), "}")
  ppt_msg(stats::setNames(lines, rep("*", length(lines))), "bullets", level = level)
}

# Classify pigs seen at several stations (misread / transfer / split).
resolve_transfers <- function(dt, qc) {
  day <- 86400
  seg_of <- function(v) {
    v[, .(start = min(entry_time), end = max(exit_time, na.rm = TRUE), n = .N),
      by = location][order(start)]
  }
  ids <- dt[identified == TRUE, .(n_loc = data.table::uniqueN(location)), by = responder]
  multi <- ids[n_loc > 1L, responder]

  stations <- dt[identified == TRUE, .(
    responder_raw = responder[1L],
    location_path = location[1L],
    main_location = location[1L],
    n_locations = 1L,
    transfer = FALSE,
    split = FALSE,
    misreads_removed = 0L,
    weight_jump_kg = NA_real_
  ), by = responder]

  misread_rows <- integer()
  new_id <- data.table::data.table(row = integer(), responder = character())
  multi_rows <- list()
  removed <- new_removed()
  dt[, row_id := .I]

  for (r in multi) {
    v <- dt[identified == TRUE & responder == r]
    seg <- seg_of(v)
    main <- seg[which.max(n), location]
    main_span <- seg[location == main]

    # 1. misreads: minor stations overlapping the main span
    n_mis <- 0L
    for (loc in setdiff(seg$location, main)) {
      s <- seg[location == loc]
      overlap <- as.numeric(difftime(min(s$end, main_span$end),
                                     max(s$start, main_span$start), units = "days"))
      if (overlap > qc$max_overlap_days) {
        rows <- v[location == loc & entry_time >= main_span$start &
                    entry_time <= main_span$end, row_id]
        misread_rows <- c(misread_rows, rows)
        n_mis <- n_mis + length(rows)
        removed <- rbind(removed, new_removed(r, loc, "prep_visits",
          sprintf("%d visits at station %s during the main station span: transponder misreads",
                  length(rows), loc)))
      }
    }
    v <- v[!row_id %in% misread_rows]
    seg <- seg_of(v)

    # 2. transfer or split, by the gap between consecutive spans
    gaps <- if (nrow(seg) > 1L) {
      as.numeric(difftime(seg$start[-1L], seg$end[-nrow(seg)], units = "days"))
    } else numeric()
    group <- cumsum(c(TRUE, gaps > qc$max_gap_days))
    seg[, group := group]
    split <- max(group) > 1L

    for (g in unique(group)) {
      sg <- seg[group == g]
      animal <- if (split) paste0(r, "_", sg$location[1L]) else r
      rows <- v[location %in% sg$location, row_id]
      new_id <- rbind(new_id, data.table::data.table(row = rows, responder = animal))

      jump <- NA_real_
      if (nrow(sg) > 1L) {
        jumps <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(sg) - 1L), function(k) {
          before <- v[location == sg$location[k] & !is.na(weight)][order(-entry_time)][seq_len(min(.N, 20L)), stats::median(weight)]
          after <- v[location == sg$location[k + 1L] & !is.na(weight)][order(entry_time)][seq_len(min(.N, 20L)), stats::median(weight)]
          after - before
        }, numeric(1))
        jump <- jumps[which.max(abs(jumps))]
        if (!is.na(jump) && abs(jump) > qc$max_jump_kg) {
          ppt_warn("Pig {.val {animal}}: body weight changes by {round(jump, 1)} kg at the station transfer {paste(sg$location, collapse = '>')}.")
        }
      }
      multi_rows[[length(multi_rows) + 1L]] <- data.table::data.table(
        responder = animal, responder_raw = r,
        location_path = paste(sg$location, collapse = ">"),
        main_location = sg[which.max(n), location],
        n_locations = nrow(sg), transfer = nrow(sg) > 1L, split = split,
        misreads_removed = n_mis, weight_jump_kg = jump
      )
    }
  }

  misread_visits <- dt[row_id %in% misread_rows]
  dt <- dt[!row_id %in% misread_rows]
  if (nrow(new_id) > 0L) {
    dt[new_id, on = c(row_id = "row"), responder := i.responder]
  }
  dt[, row_id := NULL]

  stations <- data.table::rbindlist(c(list(stations[!responder %in% multi]), multi_rows))
  data.table::setorder(stations, main_location, responder)

  n_tr <- stations[transfer == TRUE, .N]
  n_sp <- data.table::uniqueN(stations[split == TRUE, responder_raw])
  n_mr <- data.table::uniqueN(removed$responder)
  if (length(multi) == 0L) {
    ppt_msg("No pig was seen at more than one station", "info")
  } else {
    ppt_msg("{length(multi)} pig{?s} seen at several stations: {n_tr} transfer{?s}, {n_sp} split into separate animals, {n_mr} with misreads removed ({length(misread_rows)} visits)", "warning")
    if (ppt_verbose() >= 2L) {
      show <- stations[responder_raw %in% multi]
      for (i in seq_len(nrow(show))) {
        ppt_msg("{show$responder[i]}: {show$location_path[i]}{if (show$split[i]) ' (split)' else ''}{if (show$misreads_removed[i] > 0) paste0(', ', show$misreads_removed[i], ' misreads removed') else ''}", "info", level = 2L)
      }
    }
  }

  list(visits = dt, stations = stations, removed = removed,
       misread_visits = misread_visits)
}
```

```{r tests-prep_visits}
test_that("NEDAP data are standardised", {
  input <- data.table::as.data.table(nedap)
  before <- data.table::copy(input)
  v <- prep_visits(input, verbose = 0)
  expect_identical(input, before)                 # input not modified
  expect_equal(nrow(v), nrow(nedap))
  expect_equal(sum(!v$identified), 211L)
  expect_true(all(is.na(v[identified == FALSE]$responder)))
  expect_equal(sum(is.na(v$weight)), sum(nedap$weight == 0))
  expect_equal(range(v$weight, na.rm = TRUE), range(nedap$weight[nedap$weight > 0]) / 1000)
  expect_equal(v$exit_time - v$entry_time, as.difftime(v$duration, units = "secs"))
  expect_equal(attr(v, "station"), "nedap")
  expect_equal(nrow(attr(v, "stations")), 30L)
  expect_equal(min(v$seq_days), 1L)
  expect_true(all(is.na(v$trough_in)))
})

test_that("FIRE data are standardised and midnight crossings fixed", {
  v <- prep_visits(fire, verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(nrow(v), nrow(fire))
  expect_equal(sum(!v$identified), 51L)
  expect_equal(attr(v, "prep_summary")$midnight_crossings, 68L)
  expect_true(all(v$duration >= 0))
  expect_lte(max(v$duration), 3600)
  expect_equal(sum(v$feed_intake), sum(fire$Consumed) * 1000)
  expect_equal(sum(is.na(v$weight)), sum(fire$Weight == 0))
  expect_equal(nrow(attr(v, "stations")), 26L)
  expect_equal(nrow(attr(v, "removed")), 0L)
})

test_that("FIRE exit before entry beyond duration_max stays negative (OTV-lo)", {
  f <- fire[1:3, ]
  f$Entry[2] <- "14:20:00"
  f$Exit[2] <- "12:00:00"
  v <- prep_visits(f, verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(attr(v, "prep_summary")$midnight_crossings, 0L)
  expect_equal(sum(v$duration < 0), 1L)
})

test_that("sequence numbers are consistent", {
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  expect_true(all(v[identified == TRUE, all(seq_in_day == seq_len(.N)), by = .(responder, date)]$V1))
  expect_true(all(is.na(v[identified == FALSE]$seq_in_day)))
  expect_equal(v$seq_days, as.integer(v$date - min(v$date)) + 1L)
})

test_that("read_station output passes the station type on", {
  folder <- withr::local_tempdir()
  data.table::fwrite(fire, file.path(folder, "fire.csv"))
  raw <- read_station(folder, verbose = 0)
  v <- prep_visits(raw, verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(attr(v, "station"), "fire")
  expect_true("source_file" %in% names(v))
  expect_equal(sum(!v$identified), 51L)
})

# Station transfer scenarios built from one NEDAP pig
one_pig <- function() {
  d <- data.table::as.data.table(nedap)[responder == 15497]
  d[, location := 101L]
  d
}
mid_time <- function(d) d$visit_time[floor(nrow(d) / 2)]

test_that("a transfer keeps all visits with their real station", {
  d <- one_pig()
  d[visit_time > mid_time(d), location := 102L]
  v <- prep_visits(d, verbose = 0)
  st <- attr(v, "stations")
  expect_equal(nrow(st), 1L)
  expect_true(st$transfer)
  expect_false(st$split)
  expect_equal(st$location_path, "101>102")
  expect_equal(nrow(v), nrow(d))
  expect_setequal(unique(v$location), c("101", "102"))
  expect_equal(unique(v$responder), "15497")
})

test_that("a long gap splits the pig into two animals", {
  d <- one_pig()
  m <- mid_time(d)
  d <- d[visit_time < m | visit_time > m + 10 * 86400]
  d[visit_time > m, location := 102L]
  v <- prep_visits(d, verbose = 0)
  st <- attr(v, "stations")
  expect_equal(sort(st$responder), c("15497_101", "15497_102"))
  expect_true(all(st$split))
  expect_equal(v[location == "102", unique(responder)], "15497_102")
  expect_equal(unique(st$responder_raw), "15497")
})

test_that("overlapping visits at a minor station are removed as misreads", {
  d <- one_pig()
  # 30 visits spread over the whole test also recorded at station 102
  misread <- d[seq(1, .N, length.out = 30)]
  misread[, `:=`(location = 102L, visit_time = visit_time + 1)]
  v <- prep_visits(rbind(d, misread), verbose = 0)
  st <- attr(v, "stations")
  expect_equal(st$misreads_removed, 30L)
  expect_equal(unique(v$location), "101")
  expect_equal(nrow(v), nrow(d))
  expect_equal(nrow(attr(v, "removed")), 1L)
})

test_that("a weight jump at a transfer gives a warning", {
  d <- one_pig()
  m <- mid_time(d)
  d[visit_time > m, `:=`(location = 102L, weight = weight + 25000L)]
  d[visit_time > m & weight == 25000L, weight := 0L]
  expect_message(v <- prep_visits(d, verbose = 1), "transfer")
  expect_gt(attr(v, "stations")$weight_jump_kg, 10)
  expect_silent(prep_visits(d, verbose = 0))
})

test_that("bad inputs give clear errors", {
  expect_error(prep_visits(nedap, qc = list()), "qc_config")
  expect_error(prep_visits(fire, station = "nedap", verbose = 0), "visit_time")
  expect_error(prep_visits(1:3), "data.frame")
})
```

# add_breed

Pig breed (or line) usually is not in the station export and cannot be
read from the transponder number. `add_breed()` merges a breed table from
your own records into the visit table. With a `breed` column:

- `calc_adfi()` adds breed as a fixed effect to the correction model;
- `fiv_max_by_weight` limits can differ by breed;
- `calc_fcr()` summarises traits by breed.

```{r function-add_breed}
#' Add Breed Information to a Visit Table
#'
#' @description
#' Merge a table of pig IDs and breeds into a visit table from
#' [prep_visits()].
#'
#' @param visits Visit table from [prep_visits()].
#' @param breeds A data frame with one row per pig: the pig ID and its
#'   breed (or line).
#' @param id Name of the ID column in `breeds`. It is matched to the
#'   transponder number `responder_raw` (so pigs split by [prep_visits()]
#'   keep their breed), then to `responder`. Default `"responder"`.
#' @param breed Name of the breed column in `breeds`. Default `"breed"`.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details).
#'
#' @return The visit table with a `breed` column (character, `NA` for
#'   unidentified visits and for pigs not found in `breeds`). Attributes of
#'   `visits` are kept.
#' @export
add_breed <- function(visits, breeds, id = "responder", breed = "breed",
                      verbose = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  dt <- as_dt(visits, "visits")
  check_cols(dt, c("responder", "responder_raw", "identified"), arg = "visits",
             hint = "Use {.fn prep_visits} first.")
  b <- as_dt(breeds, "breeds")
  check_cols(b, c(id, breed), arg = "breeds")
  map <- unique(data.table::data.table(id = trimws(as.character(b[[id]])),
                                       breed = trimws(as.character(b[[breed]]))))
  map <- map[!is.na(id) & nzchar(id)]
  conflict <- map[, .N, by = id][N > 1L, id]
  if (length(conflict) > 0L) {
    cli::cli_abort(c("Pig{?s} with more than one breed in {.arg breeds}: {.val {conflict}}.",
                     "i" = "Keep one row per pig."))
  }
  if ("breed" %in% names(dt)) {
    ppt_msg("Replacing the existing {.field breed} column", "warning")
    dt[, breed := NULL]
  }
  dt[, breed := map$breed[match(responder_raw, map$id)]]
  dt[is.na(breed), breed := map$breed[match(responder, map$id)]]
  dt[identified == FALSE, breed := NA_character_]
  data.table::setcolorder(dt, intersect(c("responder", "responder_raw", "identified", "breed"), names(dt)))

  pigs <- unique(dt[identified == TRUE, .(responder, breed)])
  missing_pigs <- pigs[is.na(breed), responder]
  counts <- pigs[!is.na(breed), .N, by = breed][order(breed)]
  ppt_msg("Breed added for {sum(!is.na(pigs$breed))} of {nrow(pigs)} pigs: {paste0(counts$breed, ' (', counts$N, ')', collapse = ', ')}", "success")
  if (length(missing_pigs) > 0L) {
    ppt_warn("{length(missing_pigs)} pig{?s} not found in {.arg breeds}: {.val {utils::head(missing_pigs, 10)}}{if (length(missing_pigs) > 10) ' ...' else ''}")
  }
  for (a in setdiff(names(attributes(visits)), c("names", "row.names", "class", ".internal.selfref", "sorted", "index"))) {
    data.table::setattr(dt, a, attr(visits, a, exact = TRUE))
  }
  dt
}
```

```{r example-add_breed}
visits <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
# a breed table from your own herd records, one row per pig
pigs <- unique(visits[identified == TRUE, responder])
breeds <- data.frame(responder = pigs, breed = rep(c("YY", "LL"), length.out = length(pigs)))
visits <- add_breed(visits, breeds)
table(unique(visits[identified == TRUE, .(responder, breed)])$breed)
```

```{r tests-add_breed}
test_that("add_breed merges by transponder and keeps attributes", {
  v <- prep_visits(nedap, verbose = 0)
  pigs <- unique(v[identified == TRUE, responder])
  b <- data.frame(tag = pigs, line = rep(c("A", "B"), length.out = length(pigs)))
  out <- add_breed(v, b, id = "tag", breed = "line", verbose = 0)
  expect_true("breed" %in% names(out))
  expect_true(all(is.na(out[identified == FALSE, breed])))
  expect_false(anyNA(out[identified == TRUE, breed]))
  expect_equal(attr(out, "station"), "nedap")
  expect_false("breed" %in% names(v))                # input not modified
})

test_that("missing pigs warn and conflicting breeds stop", {
  v <- prep_visits(fire, verbose = 0)
  pigs <- unique(v[identified == TRUE, responder])
  expect_message(add_breed(v, data.frame(responder = pigs[1:3], breed = "YY"), verbose = 1), "not found")
  expect_error(add_breed(v, data.frame(responder = c(pigs[1], pigs[1]), breed = c("YY", "LL"))), "more than one")
  expect_error(add_breed(v, data.frame(id = pigs)), "breed")
})

test_that("split pigs keep their breed and a breed column in raw data is kept", {
  d <- data.table::as.data.table(nedap)[responder == 15497]
  d[, location := 101L]
  m <- d$visit_time[floor(nrow(d) / 2)]
  d <- d[visit_time < m | visit_time > m + 10 * 86400]
  d[visit_time > m, location := 102L]
  v <- prep_visits(d, verbose = 0)
  out <- add_breed(v, data.frame(responder = "15497", breed = "DD"), verbose = 0)
  expect_equal(unique(out$breed), "DD")
  expect_setequal(unique(out$responder), c("15497_101", "15497_102"))
  d[, breed := "LL"]
  expect_equal(unique(prep_visits(d, verbose = 0)[identified == TRUE, breed]), "LL")
  expect_message(prep_visits(nedap), "add_breed")
})
```

# clean_weight

`clean_weight()` cleans the body weight records of identified visits in
three layers:

1. **record rules**: weights outside `weight_range` are flagged;
2. **outlier detection per pig**: one or more methods fit a curve to each
   pig and flag records far from it:
   - `"rlm"`: quadratic robust regression with bisquare weights
     (`MASS::rlm`), records with weight below `rlm_cutoff` are outliers;
   - `"loess"`: robust LOESS (`family = "symmetric"`), residuals beyond
     `sd_max` robust SDs;
   - `"stl"`: STL decomposition of the daily median weight (weekly
     period, robust), residuals beyond `sd_max` robust SDs. Falls back to
     LOESS for pigs with fewer than 14 days;
   - `"sd"`: quadratic least squares, residuals beyond `sd_max` SDs;
   - optional `rel_dev_max` and `daily_drop_min` rules;
3. **pig checks**: number of valid records, test length, missing rate,
   entry and exit weight, and optionally the curve R².

Nothing is deleted silently: every record keeps a `qc_flag`, and every
removed pig is listed in `removed` with the reason.

```{r function-clean_weight}
#' Clean Body Weight Records and Check Each Pig
#'
#' @description
#' Flag implausible and outlying body weight records, then decide for each
#' pig whether its weight data are good enough for growth analysis.
#'
#' @param visits Visit table from [prep_visits()].
#' @param qc QC settings from [qc_config()]. Used here: `weight_range`,
#'   `weight_outlier`, `outlier_combine`, `rlm_cutoff`, `sd_max`,
#'   `loess_span`, `rel_dev_max`, `daily_drop_min`, `min_records`,
#'   `min_test_days`, `max_missing_rate`, `entry_weight_max`,
#'   `exit_weight_min`, `curve_r2_min`.
#' @param verbose 0 (silent), 1 (summary, default) or 2 (details).
#' @param cores Number of CPU cores for the per-pig computations. Default 1.
#'
#' @return An object of class `ppt_weight` (a list):
#'   - `per_pig`: one row per pig with `n_records`, `n_valid`,
#'     `n_outliers`, `first_date`, `last_date`, `test_days`,
#'     `missing_rate`, `entry_weight`, `exit_weight` (kg, from the fitted
#'     curve), `r2`, `status` (`"keep"`, `"low_confidence"` or
#'     `"removed"`) and `reason`;
#'   - `daily`: one row per pig and day for pigs not removed: median of the
#'     valid weights (`weight`, kg), `n_records`, `n_outliers`;
#'   - `records`: every weight record with `fitted`, `outlier` and
#'     `qc_flag` (why it was flagged);
#'   - `removed`: pigs removed here, plus misreads logged by
#'     [prep_visits()];
#'   - `settings`: the QC settings used.
#'
#' @details
#' Pig checks use the valid (non-outlier) records only:
#' - `n_valid < min_records`, `test_days < min_test_days` or
#'   `missing_rate > max_missing_rate` (share of test days without a valid
#'   weight) remove the pig;
#' - `entry_weight > entry_weight_max`, `exit_weight < exit_weight_min`,
#'   `r2 < curve_r2_min` or `max_daily_jump > max_daily_jump_kg` (the
#'   largest change of the daily median weight between consecutive recorded
#'   days, kg/d) mark the pig `"low_confidence"` but keep it: its
#'   growth can still be estimated by extrapolation in [calc_adg()], with a
#'   flag.
#'
#' @seealso [prep_visits()] for the previous step, [qc_config()] for the
#'   settings.
#' @export
clean_weight <- function(visits, qc = qc_config(), verbose = 1, cores = 1) {
  local_verbose(verbose)
  local_cores(cores)
  check_qc(qc)
  dt <- as_dt(visits, "visits")
  check_cols(dt, c("responder", "identified", "location", "date", "seq_days",
                   "entry_time", "weight"),
             arg = "visits", hint = "Use {.fn prep_visits} first.")

  ppt_msg("Cleaning body weight ({.field {paste(qc$weight_outlier, collapse = ' + ')}})", "h1")

  main_loc <- main_location(dt, attr(visits, "stations", exact = TRUE))
  rec <- dt[identified == TRUE & !is.na(weight),
            .(responder, location, date, seq_days, entry_time, weight)]
  data.table::setorder(rec, responder, entry_time)
  rec[, row_id := .I]
  rec[, qc_flag := ""]

  # 1. record rules
  rec[weight < qc$weight_range[1L] | weight > qc$weight_range[2L],
      qc_flag := "weight_range"]
  n_range <- rec[qc_flag == "weight_range", .N]

  # 2. outlier detection per pig
  fits <- fit_by_pig(rec[qc_flag == ""], detect_weight_outliers,
                     step = "clean_weight", qc = qc)
  rec[fits$result, on = "row_id", `:=`(
    fitted = i.fitted, outlier = i.outlier,
    qc_flag = data.table::fifelse(i.outlier, i.outlier_by, qc_flag)
  )]
  rec[qc_flag == "weight_range", outlier := TRUE]
  rec[is.na(outlier), outlier := FALSE]

  # 3. pig checks
  pig_fit <- unique(fits$result[, .(responder, r2, entry_weight, exit_weight)])
  per_pig <- rec[, .(
    n_records = .N,
    n_valid = sum(!outlier),
    n_outliers = sum(outlier),
    first_date = if (any(!outlier)) min(date[!outlier]) else as.Date(NA),
    last_date = if (any(!outlier)) max(date[!outlier]) else as.Date(NA),
    valid_days = data.table::uniqueN(date[!outlier])
  ), by = responder]
  # pigs whose records are all outside weight_range or that have no weight
  no_weight <- setdiff(unique(dt[identified == TRUE, responder]), per_pig$responder)
  if (length(no_weight) > 0L) {
    per_pig <- rbind(per_pig, data.table::data.table(
      responder = no_weight, n_records = 0L, n_valid = 0L, n_outliers = 0L,
      first_date = as.Date(NA), last_date = as.Date(NA), valid_days = 0L))
  }
  per_pig[, test_days := as.integer(last_date - first_date) + 1L]
  per_pig[, missing_rate := 1 - valid_days / test_days]
  per_pig <- merge(per_pig, pig_fit, by = "responder", all.x = TRUE)
  per_pig <- merge(per_pig, daily_jumps(rec), by = "responder", all.x = TRUE)
  per_pig <- merge(main_loc, per_pig, by = "responder", all.y = TRUE)
  pig_breed <- breed_of(dt)
  if (!is.null(pig_breed)) per_pig <- merge(pig_breed, per_pig, by = "responder", all.y = TRUE)

  remove_why <- pig_reasons(per_pig, qc, fits$failed, type = "remove")
  flag_why <- pig_reasons(per_pig, qc, fits$failed, type = "flag")
  per_pig[, status := data.table::fifelse(nzchar(remove_why), "removed",
                       data.table::fifelse(nzchar(flag_why), "low_confidence", "keep"))]
  per_pig[, reason := data.table::fifelse(status == "removed", remove_why, flag_why)]
  per_pig[, valid_days := NULL]
  data.table::setcolorder(per_pig, intersect(c("responder", "location", "breed"), names(per_pig)))
  data.table::setorder(per_pig, location, responder)

  kept <- per_pig[status != "removed", responder]
  rec[, kept_pig := responder %in% kept]
  daily <- rec[kept_pig == TRUE, .(
    location = location[1L],
    seq_days = seq_days[1L],
    weight = if (any(!outlier)) stats::median(weight[!outlier]) else NA_real_,
    n_records = .N,
    n_outliers = sum(outlier)
  ), by = .(responder, date)]
  data.table::setcolorder(daily, c("responder", "location", "date", "seq_days"))

  removed <- rbind(
    attr(visits, "removed", exact = TRUE) %||% new_removed(),
    per_pig[status == "removed",
            new_removed(responder, location, "clean_weight", reason)]
  )
  records <- rec[, .(responder, location, date, seq_days, entry_time, weight,
                     fitted, outlier, qc_flag)]

  report_clean_weight(rec, per_pig, n_range, fits, qc)

  new_ppt_result(per_pig = per_pig, daily = daily, removed = removed,
                 settings = qc, class = "ppt_weight") |>
    add_element(records = records)
}

# ---- helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------

`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x

# Breed of each identified pig (first non-missing value), or NULL.
breed_of <- function(dt) {
  if (!"breed" %in% names(dt)) return(NULL)
  out <- dt[identified == TRUE, .(breed = stats::na.omit(breed)[1L]), by = responder]
  out[, breed := as.character(breed)]
  out[]
}

# Largest change of the daily median valid weight between consecutive
# recorded days, in kg per day.
daily_jumps <- function(rec) {
  d <- rec[outlier == FALSE, .(w = stats::median(weight)), by = .(responder, date)]
  data.table::setorder(d, responder, date)
  d[, rate := abs(w - data.table::shift(w)) / as.numeric(date - data.table::shift(date)),
    by = responder]
  d[, .(max_daily_jump = if (all(is.na(rate))) NA_real_ else max(rate, na.rm = TRUE)),
    by = responder]
}

check_qc <- function(qc) {
  if (!inherits(qc, "ppt_qc")) {
    cli::cli_abort("{.arg qc} must be created with {.fn qc_config}.")
  }
  invisible(qc)
}

add_element <- function(x, ...) {
  extra <- list(...)
  for (nm in names(extra)) x[[nm]] <- extra[[nm]]
  x
}

# Main station of each pig: from the station history if available.
main_location <- function(dt, stations = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(stations) && all(c("responder", "main_location") %in% names(stations))) {
    out <- stations[, .(responder, location = main_location)]
  } else {
    out <- dt[identified == TRUE, .N, by = .(responder, location)][
      order(-N), .(location = location[1L]), by = responder]
  }
  unique(out, by = "responder")
}

# Robust scale: MAD, falling back to SD; NA if no spread at all.
robust_scale <- function(r) {
  s <- stats::mad(r, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(s) || s == 0) s <- stats::sd(r, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (!is.finite(s) || s == 0) NA_real_ else s
}

beyond <- function(r, k, scale) {
  if (is.na(scale)) rep(FALSE, length(r)) else abs(r) > k * scale
}

# Outlier detection for one pig. Returns one row per record.
detect_weight_outliers <- function(d, qc) {
  if (nrow(d) < 5L) {
    stop(sprintf("only %d weight records in range", nrow(d)), call. = FALSE)
  }
  t <- as.numeric(difftime(d$entry_time, min(d$entry_time), units = "days"))
  y <- d$weight
  flags <- list()
  fits <- list()

  for (m in qc$weight_outlier) {
    if (m == "rlm") {
      fit <- MASS::rlm(y ~ t + I(t^2), psi = MASS::psi.bisquare, maxit = 100)
      fits$rlm <- stats::fitted(fit)
      flags$rlm <- fit$w < qc$rlm_cutoff
    } else if (m == "loess") {
      fits$loess <- loess_fit(t, y, qc$loess_span)
      r <- y - fits$loess
      flags$loess <- beyond(r, qc$sd_max, robust_scale(r))
    } else if (m == "sd") {
      fit <- stats::lm(y ~ t + I(t^2))
      r <- stats::residuals(fit)
      fits$sd <- stats::fitted(fit)
      flags$sd <- beyond(r, qc$sd_max, stats::sd(r))
    } else if (m == "stl") {
      fits$stl <- stl_fit(t, y, qc$loess_span)
      r <- y - fits$stl
      flags$stl <- beyond(r, qc$sd_max, robust_scale(r))
    }
  }

  mat <- do.call(cbind, flags)
  outlier <- if (qc$outlier_combine == "any") rowSums(mat) > 0 else rowSums(mat) > ncol(mat) / 2
  by <- character(nrow(mat))
  for (m in colnames(mat)) by <- add_reason(by, mat[, m] %in% TRUE, m)
  ref <- fits[[1L]]

  if (!is.null(qc$rel_dev_max)) {
    rel <- abs(y - ref) / ref > qc$rel_dev_max
    by <- add_reason(by, rel, "rel_dev")
    outlier <- outlier | rel
  }
  if (!is.null(qc$daily_drop_min)) {
    drop <- daily_drop(d$date, y, outlier, qc$daily_drop_min)
    by <- add_reason(by, drop, "daily_drop")
    outlier <- outlier | drop
  }
  by[!outlier] <- ""

  # Curve on the valid records: R2 and entry/exit weight.
  ok <- !outlier
  if (sum(ok) >= 5L) {
    tt <- t[ok]
    yy <- y[ok]
    use_loess <- "loess" %in% qc$weight_outlier
    clean_fit <- if (use_loess) loess_fit(tt, yy, qc$loess_span) else stats::fitted(stats::lm(yy ~ tt + I(tt^2)))
    r2 <- 1 - sum((yy - clean_fit)^2) / sum((yy - mean(yy))^2)
    entry_weight <- clean_fit[which.min(tt)]
    exit_weight <- clean_fit[which.max(tt)]
  } else {
    r2 <- entry_weight <- exit_weight <- NA_real_
  }

  data.table::data.table(row_id = d$row_id, fitted = ref, outlier = outlier,
                         outlier_by = by, r2 = r2,
                         entry_weight = entry_weight, exit_weight = exit_weight)
}

loess_fit <- function(t, y, span) {
  fit <- stats::loess(y ~ t, span = span, degree = 2, family = "symmetric")
  stats::fitted(fit)
}

# Trend + weekly component of the daily median weight; LOESS if < 14 days.
stl_fit <- function(t, y, span) {
  day <- floor(t)
  med <- tapply(y, day, stats::median)
  days <- as.numeric(names(med))
  grid <- seq(0, max(days))
  if (length(grid) < 14L || length(days) < 7L) {
    return(loess_fit(t, y, span))
  }
  x <- stats::approx(days, med, xout = grid, rule = 2)$y
  s <- stats::stl(stats::ts(x, frequency = 7), s.window = "periodic", robust = TRUE)
  comp <- s$time.series[, "trend"] + s$time.series[, "seasonal"]
  as.numeric(comp)[day + 1L]
}

# Days whose median weight drops below `ratio` x the previous valid day.
daily_drop <- function(date, y, outlier, ratio) {
  med <- tapply(y[!outlier], date[!outlier], stats::median)
  if (length(med) < 2L) return(rep(FALSE, length(y)))
  bad_days <- names(med)[-1L][med[-1L] / med[-length(med)] < ratio]
  as.character(date) %in% bad_days
}

add_reason <- function(by, flag, label) {
  by[flag] <- ifelse(nzchar(by[flag]), paste(by[flag], label, sep = ";"), label)
  by
}

# Reasons to remove (type = "remove") or flag (type = "flag") a pig.
# Empty string = no reason.
pig_reasons <- function(p, qc, failed, type = c("remove", "flag")) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  reasons <- vector("list", nrow(p))
  add <- function(cond, text) {
    for (i in which(cond %in% TRUE)) reasons[[i]] <<- c(reasons[[i]], text[i])
  }
  if (type == "flag") {
    add(p$entry_weight > qc$entry_weight_max,
        sprintf("entry weight %.1f kg > %s kg", p$entry_weight, qc$entry_weight_max))
    add(p$exit_weight < qc$exit_weight_min,
        sprintf("exit weight %.1f kg < %s kg", p$exit_weight, qc$exit_weight_min))
    if (!is.null(qc$curve_r2_min)) {
      add(p$r2 < qc$curve_r2_min, sprintf("curve R2 %.3f < %s", p$r2, qc$curve_r2_min))
    }
    if (!is.null(qc$max_daily_jump_kg)) {
      add(p$max_daily_jump > qc$max_daily_jump_kg,
          sprintf("day-to-day weight change %.1f kg/d > %s kg/d", p$max_daily_jump, qc$max_daily_jump_kg))
    }
    return(vapply(reasons, function(x) paste(unique(x), collapse = "; "), character(1)))
  }
  add(p$responder %in% failed$responder,
      paste("curve fit failed:", failed$reason[match(p$responder, failed$responder)]))
  add(p$n_valid < qc$min_records,
      sprintf("%d valid weights < %d", p$n_valid, as.integer(qc$min_records)))
  add(p$n_valid > 0 & p$test_days < qc$min_test_days,
      sprintf("test period %d d < %d d", p$test_days, as.integer(qc$min_test_days)))
  add(p$n_valid > 0 & p$missing_rate > qc$max_missing_rate,
      sprintf("missing rate %.0f%% > %.0f%%", 100 * p$missing_rate, 100 * qc$max_missing_rate))
  vapply(reasons, function(x) paste(unique(x), collapse = "; "), character(1))
}

report_clean_weight <- function(rec, per_pig, n_range, fits, qc) {
  n_rec <- nrow(rec)
  n_out <- rec[outlier == TRUE & qc_flag != "weight_range", .N]
  method_counts <- vapply(qc$weight_outlier, function(m) {
    rec[grepl(paste0("(^|;)", m, "(;|$)"), qc_flag), .N]
  }, numeric(1))
  ppt_bullets_counts(c(
    "Weight records" = n_rec,
    "Outside weight range" = n_range,
    "Outliers" = n_out
  ))
  if (length(qc$weight_outlier) > 1L) {
    ppt_bullets_counts(stats::setNames(method_counts, paste0("  flagged by ", names(method_counts))), level = 2L)
  }
  if (nrow(fits$warnings) > 0L) {
    ppt_msg("{nrow(fits$warnings)} curve fit warning{?s} (pigs: {.val {unique(fits$warnings$responder)}})", "warning", level = 2L)
  }
  status <- per_pig[, .N, by = status]
  n_keep <- status[status == "keep", sum(N)]
  n_low <- status[status == "low_confidence", sum(N)]
  n_rm <- status[status == "removed", sum(N)]
  ppt_msg("Pigs kept: {n_keep}, low confidence: {n_low}, removed: {n_rm}",
          if (n_rm > 0L) "warning" else "success")
  if (n_rm > 0L) {
    rm <- per_pig[status == "removed"]
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(rm))) {
      ppt_msg("{.val {rm$responder[i]}} ({rm$location[i]}): {rm$reason[i]}", "danger", level = 2L)
    }
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
```
